title: Internal inflammatory root resorption
topic: Infected necrotic coronal pulp + vital apical pulp let odontoclasts balloon the canal; pulp removal stops it; 3 classic X-ray signs.

claims.claim: Internal resorption: the canal wall is resorbed from the inside (clastic activity)
claims.source: Patel S, Ricucci D, Durak C, Tay F. J Endod 2010;36:1107-21 (PMID 20630282) - abstract

claims.claim: Requirement 1: necrotic, infected pulp coronal to the lesion = the stimulus
claims.source: Abbott PV, Lin S. Dent Traumatol 2022;38:267-85 (PMID 35605161) - review full text, sect. 5

claims.claim: Requirement 2: vital pulp apical to the lesion = the blood supply
claims.source: Abbott & Lin 2022 (PMID 35605161); Patel S, Saberi N, Pimental T, Teng PH. Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - review full texts

claims.claim: Predentin lost -> dentin exposed (entry for clastic cells)
claims.source: Patel et al. Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - review full text

claims.claim: Odontoclasts resorb the dentin; the canal balloons into a symmetric oval continuous with the canal (schematic: cell number, size, route, mid-root site)
claims.source: Patel et al. 2022 (PMID 35229320) - review full text; Patel et al. 2010 (PMID 20630282) - abstract

claims.claim: Pulp out -> blood supply cut -> resorption stops (defect stays; expert consensus, no trial)
claims.source: Patel et al. 2022 (PMID 35229320) - review full text; Nilsson E et al. Int J Dent 2013;2013:929486 (PMID 24348560) - abstract

claims.claim: Perforated? Calcium silicate cement (e.g. MTA) in the defect, gutta-percha apical to it (case-report level)
claims.source: Patel et al. 2022 (PMID 35229320) - review full text

claims.claim: Classic X-ray sign 1: symmetric, well-defined ballooning
claims.source: Patel et al. 2022 (PMID 35229320), after Gartner et al. 1976 (not read); Thomas P et al. ISRN Dent 2014;2014:759326 (PMID 24944822) - review full texts

claims.claim: Classic X-ray sign 2: canal outline lost in the lesion
claims.source: Aidos H, Diogo P, Santos JM. Eur Endod J 2018;3:134-45 (PMID 32161869); Thomas et al. 2014 (PMID 24944822); Abbott & Lin 2022 - review full texts

claims.claim: Classic X-ray sign 3: stays centered on a cone shift; CBCT: perforated? (toy plan-view diagram)
claims.source: Patel et al. 2022 (PMID 35229320) - review full text; Patel S et al. Int Endod J 2009;42:831-8 (PMID 19627378) - abstract

caption:
Internal resorption: the canal wall is resorbed from the inside.
It needs both a necrotic, infected coronal pulp (the stimulus) and a vital apical pulp (the blood supply); odontoclasts work where predentin is lost. Remove the pulp and it stops, but the lost dentin is not restored. The classic 2-D signs are fallible: internal and external cervical resorption can look alike. CBCT helps and shows perforation (small studies). Evidence is mostly reviews and case reports.
